text: SC 1.1.1 (A): Every image, icon and other non-text item needs a text equivalent that does the same job; purely decorative ones get `alt=""` so screen readers skip them.
check: axe `image-alt`, `input-image-alt`, `svg-img-alt`, `role-img-alt`, `area-alt`, `object-alt`; then judge by hand whether each alt says what the image is for.

text: SC 1.2.1 (A): Recorded audio with no video needs a transcript; recorded video with no sound needs a transcript or a narration track.
check: axe none; look beside each media file for the transcript.

text: SC 1.2.2 (A): Recorded video with sound carries captions.
check: axe `video-caption` (needs review); look for `<track kind="captions">` or open captions in the picture.

text: SC 1.2.3 (A): Recorded video carries audio description or a full text alternative of what is shown.
check: axe none; list every recorded video; one with no described version, no `<track kind="descriptions">` and no linked text alternative that covers what is shown fails.

text: SC 1.2.4 (AA): Live streams with sound carry captions.
check: axe none; list live streams with sound; one with no real-time captions (a caption control or burned-in text) fails.

text: SC 1.2.5 (AA): Recorded video carries audio description (a text alternative alone no longer passes at AA).
check: axe none; list every recorded video; one whose soundtrack leaves visual information unspoken, with no described version or `<track kind="descriptions">`, fails.

text: SC 1.3.1 (A): Whatever structure the eye sees (headings, lists, tables, grouped fields, labels) must also exist in the markup or in text.
check:
axe `list`, `listitem`, `definition-list`, `td-headers-attr`, `th-has-data-cells`, `aria-required-children`, `aria-required-parent`; search for styled `
` or `

` posing as headings (axe `p-as-heading`, experimental).

text: SC 1.3.2 (A): When order carries meaning, the source and accessibility-tree order must follow the visual reading order.
check: axe none; disable CSS or walk the page with a screen reader and compare; search for `order:`, `flex-direction: *-reverse` and absolute positioning.

text: SC 1.3.3 (A): Instructions must not depend only on shape, colour, size, position, orientation or sound (for example, "the round button on the right").
check: axe none; read the UI copy.

text: SC 1.3.4 (AA): Support both portrait and landscape unless one orientation is essential to the task.
check: axe `css-orientation-lock` (experimental); search for `screenOrientation.lock`, `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations` and `android:screenOrientation`; rotate the device.

text: SC 1.3.5 (AA): Fields asking for the user's own details (name, email, tel, address...) carry the matching `autocomplete` token.
check: axe `autocomplete-valid` checks token validity only; confirm by hand that every personal-data field has one.

text: SC 1.4.1 (A): Never let colour be the sole signal for a state, error or link; add text, an icon or an underline.
check: axe `link-in-text-block`; view a greyscale screenshot.

text: SC 1.4.2 (A): Sound that starts by itself and runs more than 3 seconds needs a pause/stop control or a volume control separate from the system volume.
check: axe `no-autoplay-audio`; search for `autoplay` without `muted`.

text: SC 1.4.3 (AA): Body text needs at least 4.5:1 contrast; large text (at least 18 pt, or 14 pt bold; roughly 24 px, or 18.5 px bold) needs 3:1. Disabled controls, decoration and logos are exempt.
check: axe `color-contrast`; it cannot judge text over images or gradients, so sample those pixels yourself.

text: SC 1.4.4 (AA): Text must scale to 200 percent without assistive tech and without anything being cut off or breaking.
check: axe `meta-viewport` (flags `user-scalable=no` and `maximum-scale<2`); zoom to 200% and look for clipped or overlapping text.

text: SC 1.4.5 (AA): Render words as live text, not pictures of text, unless the user can restyle the image or the look is essential (logos count as essential).
check: axe none; look for images that contain words.

text: SC 1.4.10 (AA): At 320 CSS px wide (1280 px at 400% zoom) everything still works and scrolls in one direction only; for horizontally scrolling content (vertical text) the measure is a height of 256 CSS px. Maps, data tables, video and toolbars may scroll both ways.
check: axe none; set a 320 px viewport and look for sideways scrolling and missing content.

text: SC 1.4.11 (AA): Control edges, control states, focus rings and graphics needed for understanding need 3:1 contrast against the colours next to them.
check: axe none; measure input borders, icon buttons, toggle states and chart lines.

text: SC 1.4.12 (AA): When a user forces line height 1.5×, paragraph spacing 2×, letter spacing 0.12× and word spacing 0.16× the font size, no text or function may be lost.
check: axe `avoid-inline-spacing` (inline `!important` only); inject those values (a text-spacing bookmarklet works) and look for clipping in fixed-height boxes.

text: SC 1.4.13 (AA): Popups shown on hover or focus (tooltips, submenus) close with Esc without moving the pointer or focus, stay open while the pointer moves onto them, and stay until dismissed or no longer relevant.
check: axe none; hover, slide the pointer onto the popup, then press Esc.

text: SC 2.1.1 (A): A keyboard alone can reach and run every feature, with no need for timed keypresses.
check: axe `scrollable-region-focusable`, `frame-focusable-content`, `server-side-image-map`; put the mouse away and Tab through each flow; search for `onClick` on `div`/`span` lacking `onKeyDown`, `role` or `tabindex`.

text: SC 2.1.2 (A): Focus can always leave a component by keyboard; if leaving needs anything beyond Tab, arrows or Esc, the UI explains how.
check: axe none; Tab into embeds, editors and modals and try to get back out.

text: SC 2.1.4 (A): Shortcuts on a bare printable key (letter, digit, punctuation) can be switched off or remapped, or fire only while their component has focus.
check: axe none; search `keydown` handlers that match `e.key` against a printable character with no modifier test.

text: SC 2.2.1 (A): Each time limit can be switched off, stretched to at least 10× the default, or extended at least 10 times after a warning that leaves at least 20 seconds and needs one simple action. Exempt: real-time events, essential limits, limits over 20 hours.
check: axe `meta-refresh`; search for session timeouts, `setTimeout` redirects and countdowns.

text: SC 2.2.2 (A): Motion, blinking or scrolling that starts by itself, runs over 5 seconds and shares the screen with other content gets a pause, stop or hide control; so does auto-updating content.
check: axe `blink`, `marquee`; check carousels, tickers and autoplay video for a pause control.

text: SC 2.3.1 (A): Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second unless it stays under the general and red flash thresholds.
check: axe none; step through animation and video frame by frame.

text: SC 2.4.1 (A): Offer a way past blocks that repeat on every page: a skip link, landmarks or headings.
check: axe `bypass`; press Tab once after load and look for "Skip to content".

text: SC 2.4.2 (A): Every page has a `<title>` naming its topic or purpose, and an SPA updates it on each route change.
check: axe `document-title`; read `document.title` after each client-side navigation.

text: SC 2.4.3 (A): Tab order must keep meaning and operation intact: focus goes into a dialog when it opens and back to its trigger when it closes.
check: axe none; Tab through each page; search for `tabindex="[1-9]` (axe `tabindex`, best practice).

text: SC 2.4.4 (A): A link's text, alone or with its surrounding context, tells where it goes; a bare "Read more" with no context fails. Wording beyond the SC: TEXT-26.
check: axe `link-name` (catches empty links only); list every link text and look for identical texts leading to different places.

text: SC 2.4.5 (AA): Pages in a set can be found by at least two routes (navigation plus search, a sitemap or links); steps inside a process are exempt.
check: axe none; pick a deep page and count the routes to it (navigation, search, sitemap, table of contents, related links); a single route fails.

text: SC 2.4.6 (AA): Headings and labels say what their section or field is about.
check: axe `empty-heading` (best practice); read the heading outline and the field labels.

text: SC 2.4.7 (AA): Every keyboard-operable element shows where focus is.
check: axe none; search for `outline: none` or `outline: 0` with no `:focus-visible` style in its place; Tab and screenshot.

text: SC 2.4.11 (AA): A focused element is never completely covered by the product's own overlays: sticky headers and footers, cookie banners, chat widgets.
check: axe none; Tab down a long page with sticky bars; `scroll-padding` is the usual fix.

text: SC 2.5.1 (A): Pinch, swipe and drawn-path gestures also have a one-pointer alternative such as a button, unless the gesture is the point.
check: axe none; search for gesture handlers (`touchmove`, `PinchGesture`, `onSwipe`) and look for a matching button.

text: SC 2.5.2 (A): Single-pointer actions fire on release, or can be cancelled or undone.
check: axe none; search for actions bound to `mousedown`, `pointerdown` or `touchstart`.

text: SC 2.5.3 (A): The accessible name contains the visible label, ideally at its start; a button showing "Send" must not be named "Submit form".
check: axe `label-content-name-mismatch`; compare each `aria-label` with what is on screen.

text: SC 2.5.4 (A): Anything triggered by shaking or tilting also has an on-screen control, and the motion response can be turned off.
check: axe none; search for `devicemotion`, `deviceorientation`, `CMMotionManager` and `SensorManager`.

text: SC 2.5.7 (AA): Anything done by dragging (sortable lists, sliders, kanban) can also be done with single clicks or taps, such as buttons or a menu.
check: axe none; search for `draggable`, drag-and-drop libraries and `onDrag`.

text: SC 2.5.8 (AA): Pointer targets measure at least 24×24 CSS px; a smaller one still passes if a 24 CSS px circle centred on it overlaps no other target or circle, if another control on the page does the same job at full size, if it sits inside running text, if it is browser-drawn and unstyled, or if its size is essential or legally required. Detail: TOUCH-2.
check: axe `target-size` (it judges size and spacing only, so look for a full-size twin before reporting). Platform minimums: TOUCH-1.

text: SC 3.1.1 (A): Declare the page language on `<html lang>`.
check: axe `html-has-lang`, `html-lang-valid`.

text: SC 3.1.2 (AA): Wrap foreign-language passages in a `lang` attribute.
check: axe `valid-lang` (validity only); review by hand.

text: SC 3.2.1 (A): Focusing an element alone never navigates, submits, opens a window or moves focus elsewhere.
check: axe none; Tab through and watch for anything that fires on focus.

text: SC 3.2.2 (A): Changing a control's value never triggers such a context change (for example, a select that navigates on `change`) unless the user was warned beforehand.
check: axe none; search for `onChange` handlers that navigate or submit.

text: SC 3.2.3 (AA): Navigation repeated across pages keeps the same relative order.
check: axe none; compare the nav across several pages.

text: SC 3.2.4 (AA): The same function wears the same label and icon on every page.
check: axe none; compare labels and icons across pages.

text: SC 3.2.6 (A): Help that appears on several pages (contact details, contact form, self-help, chatbot) sits in the same relative order each time.
check: axe none; compare the pages.

text: SC 3.3.1 (A): When the system detects an input error, it points to the field and explains the problem in text.
check: axe none; submit bad data in the guarded session for client-side errors; for server-side ones fake the 400/422 with `page.route` and `route.fulfill()`, or (disposable only) submit for real; look for text by the field (a red border alone fails), plus `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.

text: SC 3.3.2 (A): Every input has a label or instructions, including any required format.
check: axe `label`, `select-name`, `form-field-multiple-labels`, `label-title-only` (best practice); flag placeholder-only fields by hand.

text: SC 3.3.3 (AA): If the fix for an error is known, the message offers it ("Enter a date like 31/12/2025").
check: axe none; trigger each validation error and read it (client-side ones in the guarded session; server-side ones via `page.route` and `route.fulfill()`, or (disposable only) for real).

text: SC 3.3.4 (AA): Submissions with legal or financial effect, that delete data, or that submit test answers must be undoable, validated with a chance to fix, or reviewed and confirmed before they are final.
check: axe none; walk the checkout, delete and transfer flows up to the final confirming step and stop ((disposable only) finish them).

text: SC 3.3.7 (A): Within one process, data the user already gave is pre-filled or offered for selection rather than asked for again (for example, billing address same as shipping).
check: axe none; walk multi-step flows and look for repeated questions.

text: SC 3.3.8 (AA): Login must not depend on a cognitive function test (recalling a password, a puzzle, retyping a code) unless there is another method, an aid such as password-manager autofill or paste, or the test is recognising objects or the user's own images.
check: axe none; search for paste blocking (`onpaste`) and `autocomplete="off"` on password and OTP fields; look for text CAPTCHAs.

text: SC 4.1.2 (A): Each UI component exposes its name and role in code, its states and values can be read and set programmatically, and changes to them are announced.
check: axe `button-name`, `link-name`, `input-button-name`, `aria-toggle-field-name`, `aria-command-name`, `aria-input-field-name`, `aria-valid-attr-value`, `aria-required-attr`, `aria-hidden-focus`, `nested-interactive`, `frame-title`; toggle each control and confirm `aria-expanded`, `aria-pressed` and `aria-selected` follow.

text: SC 4.1.3 (AA): Success notes, result counts ("3 results"), progress and errors reach screen readers without taking focus, via `role="status"`, `role="alert"`, `role="log"` or `aria-live`.
check: axe none; search toast and snackbar code for a live region that exists in the DOM before text is put into it.

text: Prefer a native element that already behaves correctly (`<button>`, `<a href>`, `<select>`, `<details>`, `<dialog>`) over a `<div>` dressed up with ARIA.
check: search for `role="button"`, `role="link"`, `role="checkbox"` and `role="tab"` on non-native elements.

text: Adding a role commits you to building all the keyboard behaviour that role implies; if you will not build it, use native HTML instead (see the APG section "No ARIA is better than Bad ARIA"). Every interactive ARIA widget must work from the keyboard.
check: for each custom `role`, try the keys listed in A11Y-60 to A11Y-66.

text: Keep `role="presentation"` and `aria-hidden="true"` off anything focusable and off its ancestors.
check: axe `aria-hidden-focus`, `presentation-role-conflict`.

text: Reserve `menu`/`menubar` for app-style command menus. Site navigation links belong in a disclosure: a `<button aria-expanded>` revealing a list of links.
check: search for `role="menu"` inside `<nav>`; where found, verify arrows move between items, Tab leaves, and Esc closes.

text: Modal dialog: opening puts focus inside; Tab and Shift+Tab cycle within it; Esc closes it; closing sends focus back to the trigger. It needs `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, a label via `aria-labelledby` on the title, and a visible close button. Only claim `aria-modal` when outside content is truly blocked (`inert` or a focus trap) and covered by a backdrop.
check: open each modal, Tab past the last control, press Esc, then inspect `document.activeElement`.

text: Menu/menubar: Tab enters and exits the whole widget rather than stepping through items; arrow keys move between items; Enter or Down Arrow opens a submenu on its first item; Esc closes the menu and puts focus back on its menu button or parent item.
check: walk each `role="menu"` with the keyboard.

text: Disclosure and accordion: Enter and Space toggle the panel; the trigger is a `button` whose `aria-expanded` flips between true and false; accordion triggers sit inside a heading.
check: confirm the trigger has `aria-expanded` and that it changes.

text: Tabs: `tablist`/`tab`/`tabpanel`; Tab lands on the active tab, and the next Tab leaves the strip; Left and Right arrows step through tabs and wrap at both ends; Home and End are optional; the active tab carries `aria-selected="true"`. Native Windows controls do not wrap (DESK-10); web tabs follow this pattern.
check: use arrows on the tab strip; Tab must not stop on each tab.

text: Combobox: the input has `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-controls` aimed at the popup; Down Arrow opens or enters the popup, Esc closes it, Enter accepts. DOM focus stays in the input while `aria-activedescendant` tracks the highlighted option.
check: type, press Down Arrow, then inspect `aria-activedescendant`.

text: Listbox: Up and Down step through options; Home and End are strongly recommended above 5 options; type-ahead is recommended above 7.
check: walk custom selects with the keyboard.

text: Alerts and toasts: an alert never grabs focus, and an important one does not vanish on a timer. Use `role="alert"` for urgent news, `role="status"` for routine updates, and an alertdialog only when the user must stop and respond.
check: search toast code for auto-dismiss timeouts; see A11Y-55.

topic: Screen reader basics (VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA, JAWS)
text: Screen reader users jump through lists of headings, landmarks, links and fields. Give each page exactly one `main`, place all content in some landmark, label repeated landmarks distinctly, and nest headings logically (one `h1`, no skipped levels).
check: axe `landmark-one-main`, `region`, `landmark-unique`, `heading-order`, `page-has-heading-one` (best practice).

topic: Screen reader basics (VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA, JAWS)
text: Each control should announce its name, role and state together ("Mute, toggle button, pressed"); an unnamed icon button is heard only as "button".
check: builds on A11Y-54; run a screen reader, Tab through, and note each announcement.

topic: Screen reader basics (VoiceOver, TalkBack, NVDA, JAWS)
text: Verify order and announcements with the real screen reader on every target platform (VoiceOver on Apple, TalkBack on Android, NVDA or JAWS on Windows); axe cannot hear speech output, live regions or lost focus.
check: run the main flow once per screen reader; on any one of them, a control read without its name, role or state, a status change not spoken, lost focus, or a reading order unlike the visual one is a finding.

text: Let the title or top heading state what the page is for, and place the key tasks where they are found first.
check: from a screenshot alone, can you say what the page does and what to do next?

text: Follow familiar layouts and hierarchies, keep visuals and control positions consistent, and make controls look clickable.
check: compare with platform conventions; look for unlabelled icons and links that look like plain text. Help placement: see A11Y-47.

text: Write in everyday, literal words, one idea per short sentence, short paragraphs and lists, with jargon and numbers explained.
check: scan the copy for idioms, double negatives and undefined terms.

text: Never make users rely on memory: signing in, signing up and resetting must not demand memorised strings, arithmetic, copying, puzzles or repeated gestures, and later steps show what earlier ones established.
check: walk the auth and multi-step flows.

text: Design forms against mistakes: collect the minimum, mark what is required, accept many formats (phone numbers, dates), offer only valid choices, and propose fixes.
check: enter valid data in an unusual format.

text: Users can step back without losing input (the browser or system Back button works) and can undo errors.
check: press Back partway through a form, then return.

text: Prefer no timeouts and autosave progress; if a limit is unavoidable, say up front how long it is and whether entries will be lost.
check: leave a form idle; see A11Y-24.

text: Native and desktop apps are judged against WCAG with "web page" read as "non-web document or software" and "web content" as "content"; most A/AA criteria then apply unchanged.
check: audit apps against A11Y-1 to A11Y-55 with that substitution.

text: A "CSS pixel" becomes the platform's density-independent unit: pt on iOS and macOS, dp on Android, epx on Windows. So SC 2.5.8 means 24×24 pt, dp or epx, and SC 1.4.10 reflow is tested at a width of 320 of those units.
check: read frame and size values in layout code.

text: SC 2.4.2 for software: where the platform supports window or screen titles, every window or screen has one naming it or its topic or purpose.
check: read window and navigation titles, or listen to the title announced on each screen.

text: SC 1.4.4 for software: text grows to 200%, or to the platform's largest text setting when that is smaller, with nothing lost (iOS Dynamic Type, Android font scale).
check: set the system font size to maximum and look for truncation.

text: SC 4.1.2 for software: name, role and value must reach the platform accessibility API, not just the screen; stock platform controls usually do this already.
check: inspect custom-drawn views with the platform accessibility inspector.

text: SC 2.4.1, 2.4.5, 3.2.3, 3.2.4 and 3.2.6 cover only a "set of software programs", which seldom exists, so they rarely bind a standalone app; consistent navigation and help across screens is still good practice.
check: do not log these as failures against a single app.

text: The European Accessibility Act (Directive (EU) 2019/882) has been in force since 28 June 2025. In scope: websites and mobile apps, e-commerce, banking, e-books, passenger transport services, computers and operating systems, smartphones, ATMs and ticketing machines. WCAG 2.2 AA failures in these products may carry legal risk in the EU.
check: does the product serve EU consumers in a covered category?

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Build controls from native elements — `<button>` and `<a>`, not clickable `<div>`/`<span>` — and where you cannot, add the right `role` and `tabindex`. Agents perceive the page through its accessibility tree; Playwright MCP works from that tree and needs no screenshots at all.
check: `playwright-cli snapshot`; a control a mouse can use that is absent from the snapshot, or appears as `generic` with no name, is broken. Grep for `onClick` on `div|span` lacking a `role`. (Accessible-name rules themselves: see a11y.md.)

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Associate each label with its input (`<label for>` or wrapping) so the snapshot shows a named textbox, not an anonymous field.
check: unnamed inputs in the snapshot; grep `<input` that has no `id` targeted by a `for=` and no `aria-label`.

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Every element a task depends on must be visible, above 8 square pixels in size, and free of transparent overlays; smaller or covered targets get dropped from a vision model's view of the page.
check: screenshot plus `snapshot --boxes` (playwright-cli 0.1.24 or later; older ones have no `--boxes`, so compare the snapshot with the screenshot by eye); zero-size, `opacity:0` or covered hit targets on a top-task path.

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Hold the layout still while the agent works: a page that keeps moving misleads screenshot-based agents, and web.dev counts elaborate hover states, moving layouts and fluid animation as things that break agents outright.
check: take two snapshots or screenshots 1 s apart with no input and diff them; list any action reachable only via `:hover` or `mouseenter`.

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Make dropdowns, scroll areas and custom widgets operable from the keyboard. Anthropic reports that Claude struggles to drive dropdowns and scrollbars with the mouse and suggests keyboard shortcuts instead.
check: finish the widget with Tab, arrows and Enter alone; custom selects that will not open from the keyboard.

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Put a separate human-confirmation step before any action with real-world effect — paying, accepting terms, giving consent — that an agent cannot fold into the action itself. Anthropic tells deployers to get human sign-off for payments and terms acceptance, and to check before each batch, since one batch can finish a multistep action in a single turn.
check: walk checkout, delete and terms flows in the snapshot up to the final click and stop there ((disposable only) press it); a single click that spends money or deletes data without a review state is a finding.

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Show the result of each action on the page (status message, changed heading, new row). Claude can assume an action worked without looking, so a silent success or failure reaches the user as a wrong report.
check: diff the snapshot after each step of the walk; no visible change means the agent has nothing to verify against.

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: Treat page content as a prompt-injection channel: text on a page or in an image can redirect an agent away from its instructions. Keep user-generated content visibly apart from controls and never present it as instructions.
check: can user-supplied text (reviews, names, comments) land beside or inside action labels in the snapshot?

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: (Draft) If the product wants agents to call declared tools instead of clicking, register them with WebMCP: `document.modelContext.registerTool()` with `name`, `description`, `inputSchema` and annotations such as `readOnlyHint` and `consequentialHint`. WebMCP is a Draft Community Group Report, not a W3C Standard, and web.dev warns the API is still changing.
check: `typeof document.modelContext` in the console; list the registered tools and apply AGENT-11-AGENT-16 to them.

topic: Web UI for browser and computer-use agents
text: A bot wall or CAPTCHA that stops an agent the user has authorised, with no other route for it (an API, an MCP server, verified-agent signing), is a finding; report the step and leave the trade-off against abuse to the owner. A draft route to verified agents exists: the IETF Web Bot Auth Internet-Draft has agents sign requests (`Signature-Agent` header, keys at `/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory`, `tag` set to `web-bot-auth`), and it is still a work in progress.
check: during the agent walk, note whether and at which step a challenge page appears; a challenge with no alternative route for agents fails.

text: Offer a small set of tools shaped around user tasks rather than mirroring each endpoint; give each one a single, non-overlapping job — e.g. one `schedule_event` that both finds a free slot and books it. Merge related operations into one tool with an `action` parameter.
check: read `tools/list`; overlapping tools, or a common user task that takes several chained low-level calls, is a finding.

text: Prevent name collisions by prefixing tools with service or resource (`asana_search`, `github_list_prs`). MCP: names SHOULD be 1-128 characters, case-sensitive, limited to A-Z, a-z, 0-9, `_`, `-` and `.`, and unique per server. Claude API: `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$`.
check: run the regex over every tool name; flag bare names such as `search` or `get`.

text: Describe each tool the way you would brief a new colleague: its job, when to pick it and when not to, what every parameter does, and what it leaves out. Anthropic's target is 3-4 sentences or more per description.
check: count sentences per description; a one-line description that only restates the tool name fails.

text: Give parameters unambiguous names (`user_id` rather than `user`) and pin them down in a typed schema with enums, required fields and formats. Shape arguments so mistakes are hard to make, e.g. insist on absolute file paths. A tool without parameters should use `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":false}` per MCP.
check: `inputSchema` `string` properties lacking `description`, `enum` or `format`; parameters called `data`, `input`, `user` or `id`.

text: Return just the fields the next step needs, using meaningful, stable identifiers instead of opaque ones; drop technical fields like `uuid`, `256px_image_url` and `mime_type` unless they are needed. Add a `response_format` enum (`"concise"`/`"detailed"`) when callers need different depths.
check: call a list tool and count fields an agent will never use; ids without a readable name alongside.

text: Cap response size through pagination, ranges, filters or truncation; when you truncate, say so and explain how to narrow the request. Claude Code limits a tool response to 25,000 tokens by default. MCP lists page with an opaque `cursor`/`nextCursor`.
check: run the widest query; an unbounded dump, or a silent cut with no "N more, filter by X" hint, is a finding.

text: Put tool failures in the tool result with `isError: true` and a message that says how to fix the call — not in a protocol-level error, which the model never sees and so cannot recover from. Input-validation failures go here too (e.g. "Start date must be after today; today is 2026-11-11"). Avoid bare error codes and tracebacks.
check: call every read-only tool (read-only by its code, not just `readOnlyHint`) with a wrong type, an out-of-range value and a missing field, and read the reply; (disposable only) do the same with write tools, since a broken validator lets the bad call write — read-only: read their validation code and `inputSchema`.

text: Set MCP annotations honestly: `readOnlyHint` (default false), `destructiveHint` (default true, only meaningful for non-read-only tools), `idempotentHint` (default false), `openWorldHint`. Clients MUST treat annotations from untrusted servers as untrusted, so they never stand in for server-side checks.
check: a delete/send/pay tool without annotations or with `destructiveHint:false`; a read tool lacking `readOnlyHint:true`.

text: For structured results, declare an `outputSchema`, return `structuredContent` that matches it (a MUST for servers), and repeat it as serialized JSON in a text block for older clients.
check: call a read-only tool ((disposable only) a write tool) and validate its `structuredContent` against its `outputSchema`.

text: Return HTTP API errors as RFC 9457 Problem Details (`application/problem+json`, with `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, `instance`), and aim `detail` at telling the client how to fix the request, not at debugging output.
check: `curl -i` a malformed read (a bad query parameter, an unknown id); (disposable only) a malformed `POST` or `PUT`; HTML error pages, bare 500s or stack traces in the body are findings.

text: Make retries harmless with an idempotency key on every create and update (Stripe: `Idempotency-Key` header on `POST`, keys up to 255 characters, eligible for removal after 24 hours, rejected when reused with different parameters). Flag idempotent MCP tools with `idempotentHint`.
check: (disposable only) send one create twice with the same key; two resulting objects mean a retrying agent duplicates charges or records. Read-only: find the `Idempotency-Key` handling in the code or OpenAPI description; a create with none fails.

text: Throttle with `429 Too Many Requests`, an explanation in the body, and a `Retry-After` header giving the wait. MCP servers MUST rate limit tool calls.
check: (disposable only) burst until throttled; a 429 lacking `Retry-After`, or throttling that surfaces as a 500 or a hang, is a finding. Read-only: read the rate-limit middleware or config and the documented 429 body and `Retry-After`.

text: Publish an OpenAPI description so people and programs can learn what the API does without reading its code; every `operationId` MUST be unique across the API, and each operation needs a `summary`/`description`.
check: fetch the description and lint it; flag operations without `operationId` or `description`.

text: Write results to stdout and logs and errors to stderr; exit 0 on success and non-zero on failure.
check: `cmd >/dev/null` should leave only diagnostics; force a failure with an unknown flag or a missing argument, then `echo $?`.

text: Support machine-readable output: emit formatted JSON under `--json`, and offer `--plain` when decorated output would break parsing.
check: `cmd --json | jq.` for each read command.

text: Prompt only when stdin is an interactive terminal; otherwise demand the values as flags or arguments, and treat `--no-input` as a ban on all interaction.
check: `cmd </dev/null` on a read command, and on a write command with a `--dry-run` that its own `--help` documents and its code stops on before any write, or (disposable only) with none; hanging or waiting at a prompt is a finding.

text: Guard dangerous operations in a scriptable way: without a TTY, require `-f`/`--force` or `--confirm="name-of-thing"`; offer `--dry-run` to report what would change without changing it.
check: (disposable only) run the delete command with stdin closed; it must refuse without `--force` and must not prompt. Read-only: its `--help` lists `--force` (or `--confirm`) and `--dry-run`, the code refuses without a TTY, and the code shows `--dry-run` returns before any write.

text: Show help for `-h` and `--help`; drop animations when stdout is not a TTY; respect `NO_COLOR`; provide `-q`.
check: `cmd --help`; `cmd | cat` for spinner or ANSI leftovers; `NO_COLOR=1 cmd`.

text: Keep operations idempotent where you can, and catch expected errors to replace them with a message that says what to do next.
check: (disposable only) run the same create/apply twice — read-only: read the apply code for an idempotency check, or use a `--dry-run` that its own `--help` documents and its code stops on before any write; read the error for a missing argument.

text: Take secrets from a file or stdin (e.g. `--password-file`), not from a flag value.
check: `--help` for `--token`/`--password` flags that take the secret inline.

text: (Proposal) Serve `/llms.txt`: Markdown with an H1 naming the project (the one required part), a blockquote summary, H2 sections of link lists, and an "Optional" H2 for links an agent may skip. The llms.txt proposal is at version 2 and still open for community input.
check: `curl -sf https://<host>/llms.txt`; a 404 or HTML is a finding; verify the H1 and that links resolve.

text: (Proposal) Publish a clean Markdown copy of each doc page at its URL plus `.md` (`page.html.md` or `page.md`; `index.html.md` for directory URLs).
check: `curl -sf <doc-url>.md`.

text: For a code product, keep agent instructions in `AGENTS.md` at the repo root — build and test commands, code style, testing, security notes. In a monorepo, add one per package; agents use the nearest file up the tree.
check: `ls AGENTS.md`; confirm its build and test commands run.

text: Document example calls, edge cases and input formats for tools and APIs; give complex tools schema-valid `input_examples`. Prefer formats that are common in ordinary text on the web over bespoke ones.
check: run each documented read example exactly as written; (disposable only) the examples that write — read-only: validate them against the schema or OpenAPI description; a broken example sends an agent into a retry loop.

text: Let agents sign in with scoped, audience-bound tokens instead of the user's password. MCP over HTTP: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, Protected Resource Metadata and `resource` indicators; tokens MUST NOT go in the URI query string; reject tokens minted for another audience; never forward a received token; 401 for invalid tokens, 403 for missing scope; short-lived access tokens. Anthropic advises keeping login credentials away from computer-use models.
check: `curl -i` the MCP endpoint without a token — expect 401 with `WWW-Authenticate`; can an agent be granted less than full account access?

text: Keep a human able to refuse tool calls: show which tools the model can use, mark visibly when one runs, show its inputs before the call, and ask for confirmation on sensitive operations.
check: (disposable only) trigger a destructive tool in the client or host UI; it must show the inputs and wait for approval, then decline it. Read-only: read the host's approval setting for that tool.

text: Record agent actions in an audit log (an MCP client SHOULD log tool use for audit) and tie each entry to both the agent and the user it acted for.
check: (disposable only) act through the API/MCP, then find that action in the product's activity or audit log. Read-only: read the code that writes the audit entry; it must record both the agent and the user.

text: Make agent output easy to hand over: a shareable result the user can claim into their own account in one step, as with Netlify's one-click site claiming.
check: (disposable only) after an agent creates something, can the human find it, claim it and take over without the agent? Read-only: read the docs or code for a claim or transfer flow.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: Pick the layout from the window size class, not from what kind of device it is. Width: compact < 600dp, medium 600-840dp, expanded 840-1200dp, large 1200-1600dp, extra-large ≥ 1600dp. Height: compact < 480dp, medium 480-900dp, expanded ≥ 900dp.
check: grep `isTablet|smallestScreenWidthDp|Build.MODEL|resources.getBoolean(R.bool.is_tablet` deciding layout; a device check standing in for a size class is the bug.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: Recompute the layout every time the window size moves (rotation, fold/unfold, split-screen or desktop resize); the class can change while the app runs.
check: size class computed once in `onCreate` or cached; drag-resize in the resizable emulator and look for a layout that does not follow.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: Look at height as well: phones turned to landscape tend to be medium wide yet compact tall (< 480dp), too short for two panes.
check: landscape phone screenshot; a two-pane or tall header layout that squeezes content out.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: Occupy the full window, without letterboxing or compatibility mode, and keep every piece of content inside it.
check: manifest `android:resizeableActivity="false"`, fixed `android:screenOrientation`, `maxAspectRatio`; black bands on a tablet or open foldable. Large screens (sw ≥ 600dp) on Android 12+ allow every orientation whatever `screenOrientation` says, and multi-window even with `resizeableActivity="false"`, so test both.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: Preserve what the user was doing across configuration changes: list scroll offset, typed text and keyboard state, playback position; this must hold for rotation, fold/unfold, window resize and any sequence of them.
check: fill fields, scroll, start media, then rotate, resize and fold in turn; anything that resets fails (T-Config_State, T-Config_Combinations).

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: Where content allows, use a canonical multi-pane layout: list-detail (messaging, contacts, media browsing), supporting pane (document beside comments, video beside related items), feed (a grid whose column count follows width).
check: at expanded width, one stretched column or a phone layout floating in empty space. Compose: `ListDetailPaneScaffold`, `SupportingPaneScaffold`, `LazyVerticalGrid(GridCells.Adaptive(...))`; Views: Activity embedding.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: List-detail shows both panes at expanded width and one pane at medium/compact, with Back going from detail to list. Carry the selection through width changes: going narrow keeps the open detail, going wide highlights the item it belongs to.
check: open an item, resize compact to expanded and back; a lost selection or the wrong pane is a fail.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: Place a supporting pane by width: under the main content or in a bottom sheet at compact, half and half at medium, 70% main / 30% supporting at expanded.
check: one screenshot per size class.

topic: Window size classes and adaptive layout
text: On big windows, constrain secondary UI: bottom sheets, buttons and text fields keep a sensible width, small menus and modals leave the screen visible, context menus appear beside the item tapped, images keep their proportions and are not cropped.
check: expanded-width screenshot; a button or text field spanning a whole tablet. MDC `BottomSheet` default `android:maxWidth` is 640dp.

text: Adapt to tabletop posture (calls, playback) and book posture (long-form reading); in tabletop, move controls like media transport onto the flat lower half.
check: Pixel Fold emulator half-open; controls sitting across the hinge.

text: Work completely in multi-window with multi-resume: an unfocused window keeps updating (playback, incoming messages, progress), and camera and mic are given up and taken back cleanly.
check: split-screen with the other app focused; stalled content or a camera that never recovers (T-Multi-Window_Focus, T-Multi-Window_Resources).

text: Take text from a hardware keyboard and move between hardware and on-screen keyboards with no activity restart.
check: plug and unplug a keyboard while typing; a relaunch or vanished text.

text: Handle a mouse or trackpad for the basics: clicking anything clickable, selecting text by dragging or double-clicking, scrolling lists and pickers vertically and horizontally.
check: operate each screen with a mouse on ChromeOS or the Desktop emulator.

text: Let users complete the main flows with Tab and arrow keys, and show a visible focus state on every interactive custom drawable outside touch mode.
check: Tab across a screen; focus that disappears, jumps over controls or cannot be seen (Keyboard_Navigation, Drawable_Focus).

text: Honour expected keys: Ctrl shortcuts for select, cut, copy, paste, undo, redo; Space toggles playback; Enter sends in messaging apps; Esc backs out (closes dialogs, menus and pop-ups, clears search, leaves full screen, abandons an edit).
check: try each key on a hardware keyboard; no `onKeyEvent`/`onKeyDown` handling for Esc and Enter.

text: Show hover feedback on actionable elements, open context menus from right-click or two-finger tap, and support zoom with Ctrl+scroll and pinch on a trackpad.
check: hover and right-click with a mouse; no response.

text: Let a stylus pick, scroll and handwrite into text fields (on Android 14+ `EditText` accepts handwriting out of the box, with no soft keyboard popping up).
check: a home-made text input drawn on a plain `View`/`Canvas` that ignores stylus writing.

text: Lay out edge-to-edge and add padding for insets. Targeting SDK 35 makes edge-to-edge mandatory on Android 15+; older versions need `enableEdgeToEdge()`.
check: `targetSdk >= 35` but no `WindowInsets`/`setOnApplyWindowInsetsListener`/`safeDrawingPadding`; a FAB, bottom bar or final list row under the navigation bar.

text: Pad tappable views clear of `WindowInsetsCompat.Type.systemBars()`, pad lists clear of `displayCutout()`, and keep swipe surfaces out of `systemGestures()` zones.
check: screenshots in gesture and 3-button nav, portrait and landscape on a device with a cutout; a carousel or sheet that competes with the back swipe.

text: Let lists scroll behind the navigation bar but still reach their last row: add bottom padding and `clipToPadding="false"`.
check: scroll to the bottom; the last row stays hidden.

text: Leave the gesture nav bar see-through with no fill; a translucent scrim belongs only behind 3-button nav over scrolling content. Choose light or dark status bar icons to stand out from the content underneath.
check: solid colored bar behind the gesture handle; light icons over a light app bar (`isAppearanceLightStatusBars`).

text: Move the layout in step with the keyboard animation and keep the active field above the IME (`WindowInsetsAnimationCompat`).
check: tap the lowest field; it ends up under the keyboard or the layout snaps.

text: Route Back through `OnBackPressedCallback`/`BackHandler`/`PredictiveBackHandler` (AndroidX Activity 1.6.0+) rather than an `onBackPressed` override or `KEYCODE_BACK` interception. Predictive back is enabled by default.
check: grep `override fun onBackPressed|onBackPressed()|KEYCODE_BACK`; `android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false"` in the manifest turns the system animations off.

text: Turn a back callback on only while there is UI to unwind (unsaved form, open sheet, detail pane), tied to observable state; logging or business logic belongs elsewhere, because a consuming callback kills the back-to-home preview.
check: a callback that is always enabled or fires analytics; a back swipe at the root with no home preview.

text: Back should first close a modal bottom sheet, dialog or search, then navigate. MDC modal sheets get predictive back for free; a standard sheet needs an `OnBackPressedCallback` that hands events to `BottomSheetBehavior`.
check: open a sheet and press Back; the screen underneath pops instead.

text: Show a navigation bar when width or height is compact (or in tabletop posture) and a navigation rail otherwise; expanded widths may use an expanding rail or a permanent drawer. Drawers on large screens give way to expanded rails.
check: a bottom bar stretched across a landscape tablet; neither `NavigationSuiteScaffold` nor a manual switch.

text: A navigation bar carries three to five destinations and a collapsed rail three to seven; each item has an `android:title` for TalkBack.
check: count items; `BottomNavigationView` refuses more than 5; icon-only items without a title.

text: Reserve the FAB for the screen's main or most frequent action, and label an icon-only FAB with `contentDescription`.
check: several FABs on a screen; `FloatingActionButton` lacking `android:contentDescription` (Compose `Icon(..., contentDescription = null)` in a FAB).

text: Keep dialogs rare and for things that need an answer now; they halt the app until the user accepts, cancels or acts. A multi-step task gets a full-screen dialog.
check: dialogs for tips or success notices; a title icon with no content description.

text: Use a snackbar for short, non-blocking feedback (offer Undo after something destructive); never stack them; anchor them above the FAB or bottom navigation.
check: snackbar on top of the bottom nav or FAB (no `setAnchorView`/`Scaffold` `snackbarHost`); a critical error shown only as a snackbar.

text: Timed UI that holds controls (an action snackbar, self-hiding player controls) stays up for at least `AccessibilityManager.getRecommendedTimeoutMillis()`; an important snackbar action can use `SnackbarDuration.Indefinite` / `LENGTH_INDEFINITE` plus a dismiss action.
check: fixed `postDelayed`/`delay()` hide timers; `LENGTH_SHORT` on a snackbar with Undo.

text: Set `android:inputType` on each `EditText` (`phone`, `textEmailAddress`, `textPassword`, `number`...) to get the matching keyboard and masked passwords.
check: lint `TextFields`; `EditText` with no `inputType`; an email field that opens the plain text keyboard.

text: Give each field the IME action that fits it (`imeOptions` `actionNext`, `actionDone`, `actionSend`, `actionSearch`) and act on it.
check: the final field offers Next and nothing happens; a search box with no `actionSearch`.

text: Tag autofillable fields with `android:autofillHints` / `HintConstants.AUTOFILL_HINT_*`, and keep `importantForAutofill="no"` off password and card fields.
check: lint `Autofill`; login fields lacking `password`/`username`; a sign-up form using `password` where `newPassword` belongs.

text: Tie a visible label to every field (Views `android:labelFor`; Compose `TextField(label =...)`); placeholder text shows example input and does not count as the label.
check: lint `LabelFor`; TalkBack says "Edit box" with no name.

text: Ask for a runtime permission at the moment the user reaches for the feature that needs it (general rule: WEB-42); when `shouldShowRequestPermissionRationale()` is true, explain first in a screen the user can dismiss.
check: permission prompts in the launcher activity's `onCreate` or a splash; an explanation with no way out.

text: After a denial, keep going: leave the rest of the app working, explain in the spot where the missing result would show exactly which feature is off, no blocking full-screen warning, no repeated pleading. A second denial makes the system dialog stop appearing.
check: deny and carry on; a dead end, a loop back to the prompt, or recurring "please enable" dialogs. `adb shell dumpsys package <pkg>` shows `USER_FIXED`.

text: On Android 13+, request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` in response to something the user did that implies wanting updates (subscribing, tracking an order), not on first launch, and test `areNotificationsEnabled()` before depending on notifications.
check: `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` requested at startup; reset with `adb shell pm revoke <pkg> android.permission.POST_NOTIFICATIONS` and relaunch clean.

text: Give every kind of notification its own channel, with a readable name and description and an importance matching how urgent it is; offer a shortcut to `ACTION_CHANNEL_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS` in the app's settings.
check: a single channel for everything; promotions at `IMPORTANCE_HIGH`.

text: Support dark theme (Android 10+): base the theme on `DayNight` and take colors from theme attributes or `-night` resources instead of literals; offer Light / Dark / System default, defaulting to System default (the platform split: VIS-36).
check: grep `#FFFFFF|Color.White|Color(0xFF` for backgrounds and text in layouts and composables; `adb shell cmd uimode night yes`, then screenshot.

text: Theme widgets, custom notification layouts and the launch screen too; prefer system notification templates such as `MessagingStyle`.
check: a white splash or widget in dark mode; drawables with baked-in colors.

text: With dynamic color (Android 12+, `DynamicColors.applyToActivitiesIfAvailable`, Compose `dynamicLightColorScheme`/`dynamicDarkColorScheme`), color by role tokens and pull brand colors into the palette with `HarmonizedColors` so contrast survives any wallpaper.
check: literal colors next to dynamic roles; text on `primary` that is not `onPrimary`.

text: Express text size and `lineHeight` in `sp`, not `dp`/`px`, so the user's font setting takes effect; Android 14 scales fonts up to 200%, nonlinearly.
check: lint `SpUsage`; grep XML `textSize="[0-9.]+(dp|dip|px)"` and `lineHeight="[0-9.]+dp"`; `setTextSize(TypedValue.COMPLEX_UNIT_(DIP|PX)`.

text: Skip arithmetic on `fontScale` or `scaledDensity`, which nonlinear scaling made unreliable; convert with `TypedValue.applyDimension()`/`deriveDimension()`, and keep `sp` out of padding and fixed heights.
check: grep `scaledDensity|fontScale \*|\* fontScale`; hard `layout_height`/`Modifier.height(` on text containers.

text: Walk every screen at 200% font size: text must not truncate, clip or overlap and every control must stay reachable.
check: `adb shell settings put system font_scale 2.0`, screenshot each screen, set back to `1.0`.

text: Make every interactive element at least 48dp × 48dp to touch (Material components already are; custom clickables need `sizeIn(minWidth = 48.dp, minHeight = 48.dp)` or `minimumInteractiveComponentSize()`). touch.md owns target sizing in depth.
check: grep `Modifier.*clickable` near `.size\((1?[0-9]|[2-3][0-9]|4[0-7])\.dp\)`; Accessibility Scanner "Touch target".

text: Every meaningful image and icon-only control gets a localized `contentDescription` naming what it does, not what it is ("Share", not "Share button"); only decorative images get `null` (Compose) or `importantForAccessibility="no"` (Views).
check: lint `ContentDescription`; grep `contentDescription = null` within `IconButton`/`clickable`/FAB; `contentDescription = ""`; descriptions that end in "button" or "icon".

text: Make each list item's description distinct by folding in its own data, so a row of "Delete" or "Play" buttons can be told apart.
check: TalkBack down a list; every row sounds the same.

text: Collapse related bits into a single focus stop (Compose `semantics(mergeDescendants = true)`; Views `screenReaderFocusable="true"` on the container), and make only the container clickable.
check: TalkBack lands separately on a card's avatar, name and time; clickables nested in a clickable row.

text: Flag headings (`semantics { heading() }` / `android:accessibilityHeading`) and name separate panes with distinct titles (`paneTitle` / `android:accessibilityPaneTitle`).
check: TalkBack jump-by-heading finds none; the same vague pane title reused across screens.

text: Offer each gesture-only action (swipe to dismiss, drag to reorder, long press) as a labelled accessibility action (`customActions`, `onClickLabel`/`onLongClickLabel`; `ViewCompat.addAccessibilityAction`/`replaceAccessibilityAction`).
check: TalkBack says "Double tap and hold to long press"; swipe-to-delete missing from the TalkBack actions menu.

text: Expose role and state on custom controls (`Role.Switch`, `stateDescription`, `toggleable`/`triStateToggleable`), or subclass the nearest framework widget.
check: a custom toggle read as plain text with no on/off; `Modifier.clickable` on something that looks like a checkbox, with no `role`.

text: Make TalkBack and keyboard order follow how the screen reads; repair column or circular layouts with `isTraversalGroup`/`traversalIndex` (Views `accessibilityTraversalBefore/After`).
check: TalkBack hops between columns; an Accessibility Test Framework result on traversal order.

text: Text contrast of 4.5:1 or more below 18sp (or bold below 14sp), 3:1 or more above, which matches WCAG (A11Y-14 owns contrast); state is never shown by color alone (A11Y-12).
check: Accessibility Scanner "Low contrast"; an error marked only in red.

text: Any view that overrides `onTouchEvent` or sets `setOnTouchListener` must also wire `performClick()`; custom widgets must be keyboard reachable.
check: lint `ClickableViewAccessibility`, `KeyboardInaccessibleWidget`.

text: Lay out content and controls within the safe area, so nothing important sits under the Dynamic Island, status bar, toolbar or tab bar.
check: screenshot a Dynamic Island device in portrait and landscape; grep `.ignoresSafeArea(` / `edgesIgnoringSafeArea` on views that contain controls; UIKit constraints pinned to the view edge rather than `safeAreaLayoutGuide`.

text: Drive layout decisions from size classes; device model and orientation say nothing about the space actually available.
check: grep `userInterfaceIdiom ==.pad`, `UIDevice.current.orientation`, `UIScreen.main.bounds` used for layout; the fix reads `horizontalSizeClass` / `UITraitCollection`.

text: Every compact/regular combination must render well, and changing size class (rotation, resizing, iPad windows) must never remove a feature.
check: screenshots at compact and regular width, portrait and landscape, plus a narrow iPad window; a feature reachable in one and gone in another fails.

text: An app that supports both orientations opens in whichever one the device is in; a landscape-only app works with the device turned either way.
check: launch while holding the device each way; inspect `supportedInterfaceOrientations` / `UISupportedInterfaceOrientations`.

text: At big text sizes, rearrange rather than clip: stack items that sat side by side and let rows get taller.
check: set `accessibility-extra-extra-extra-large` (see Measure) and screenshot; overlapping or cut-off text fails.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: Handle any window size gracefully: iPad apps may be windowed and freely resized as on a Mac, and the app is not told which arrangement the person picked.
check: drag the window to its smallest size and back to full screen; broken or letterboxed layout fails.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: When the person leaves a game or a video, stop it, and pick up at the same point when they return.
check: background the app mid-video or mid-level and come back; lost progress fails.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: Standard buttons and text areas get the system pointer effects; leave roughly 12 pt around bezeled elements and roughly 24 pt around unbezeled ones, and make the hit areas of adjacent custom bar buttons touch with no dead gaps.
check: hover with a trackpad on device or in Simulator; custom controls with no highlight or lift fail; grep custom controls missing `.hoverEffect(` / `UIPointerInteraction` / `isPointerInteractionEnabled`.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: Everything works from a hardware keyboard with Full Keyboard Access, and the familiar shortcuts (Cmd-C/V/Z/F/N/W, Esc to cancel) keep their usual meaning.
check: attach a keyboard, turn on Settings > Accessibility > Keyboards > Full Keyboard Access, and reach every control; grep `UIKeyCommand(` / `.keyboardShortcut(` binding a standard key to an unrelated action.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: Each custom key command carries a title, so iPad lists it in the shortcut overlay and the menu bar.
check: grep `UIKeyCommand(` lacking `title:`/`discoverabilityTitle`; hold Cmd on iPad and look for it.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: Menu bar commands on iPad also need an on-screen route: the menu bar is usually hidden in full screen, and dynamic items need a hardware keyboard.
check: list `CommandMenu`/`UIMenuBuilder` items; any command with no equivalent in the visible UI fails.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: A Pencil stroke draws the instant the tip lands, with no button or mode to enable first; Pencil hover and double tap never change content.
check: open a canvas and draw straight away; grep `UIPencilInteraction` handlers that delete or alter content.

topic: iPadOS: multitasking, windows, pointer, keyboard, Pencil
text: Scribble should work wherever writing text makes sense, and a field must hold still (no autoscroll) while someone writes in it.
check: handwrite into each text field and custom text view; grep `UIScribbleInteraction` that turns it off.

text: Tabs switch between top-level areas only; commands belong in a toolbar. An iPad app with many areas can use a tab bar that turns into a sidebar, kept to two levels at most.
check: a tab that performs a command or opens a sheet fails; a sidebar three levels deep fails.

text: The tab bar stays on screen in every section (a modal may cover it), and tabs are never hidden or greyed out; an empty section says why it is empty.
check: walk each tab and push detail views; a tab bar that vanishes on push, or a disabled tab, fails; grep `.toolbar(.hidden, for:.tabBar)`, `hidesBottomBarWhenPushed`.

text: Each tab shows a brief text label, ideally a single word, alongside its icon.
check: screenshot the tab bar; grep `tabItem { Image(` with no `Text`/`Label`.

text: Rely on the system Back and Close controls with their standard symbols rather than text buttons reading "Back" or "Close", and leave the edge swipe back intact.
check: grep `navigationBarBackButtonHidden(true)`, `hidesBackButton = true`, custom leading "Back" buttons; try the edge swipe in Simulator.

text: Custom shortcut gestures add to the standard ones and never take their place; system gestures such as three-finger undo/redo and screen-edge swipes keep their meaning.
check: grep `DragGesture`/`UIScreenEdgePanGestureRecognizer` attached to screen edges; try a three-finger swipe while editing text.

text: After a relaunch, bring people back to the screen, scroll offset and windows they had.
check: go several levels deep, kill the app (`simctl terminate`), relaunch; starting over at the root fails.

text: Every modal must be easy to leave: on iOS/iPadOS that means a button in its top toolbar plus swiping it down.
check: open each sheet and full-screen cover; no Cancel/Close and no swipe-down fails; grep `interactiveDismissDisabled()` / `isModalInPresentation = true` with no visible way out.

text: If closing a modal would throw away what the person typed, stop and ask first (for example an action sheet with a save option), for both swipe and button.
check: type into a sheet and swipe it away; losing the input silently fails.

text: Never stack sheets: dismiss the current one before another appears.
check: any flow where a sheet opens on top of a sheet fails.

text: In a single-view sheet, Cancel sits at the leading edge and Done at the trailing edge; Done always has a Cancel or Back partner, and the three never appear together.
check: screenshot each sheet's toolbar.

text: Button hit regions follow TOUCH-1: Apple's default control size is 44×44 pt on iOS/iPadOS with a 28×28 pt minimum, and 28×28 pt on macOS with a 20×20 pt minimum. Spacing: TOUCH-4.
check: Accessibility Inspector "Hit region" audit; grep `.frame(width:` on buttons: under the minimum fails, between minimum and default is a weaker finding.

text: Custom buttons visibly react when pressed, and a button that starts slow work shows a spinner until it finishes.
check: press and hold a custom button; on a slow network (SKILL.md: Slow network), tap an action that hits the network — a read (refresh, search, open), or (disposable only) one that writes — and watch for feedback. Loading and progress beyond the spinner: WEB-60 to WEB-66.

text: The visually prominent (primary) role goes to a safe option, never to a destructive one, however likely people are to pick it.
check: grep `.buttonStyle(.borderedProminent)` / `.keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction)` on delete or erase buttons.

text: Keep alerts for things that truly matter: not for routine deletions people can undo, and not on launch (report problems such as being offline with a quiet inline label).
check: launch with no network; an alert on startup fails; an alert in front of a routine, undoable delete fails ((disposable only) to delete for real; read-only: grep the delete path for `.alert(`).

text: Name alert buttons after what they do ("Delete", "Erase"); "OK" only fits a purely informational alert. Any alert with a destructive choice also offers Cancel.
check: grep `Alert(`/`.alert(`/`UIAlertAction(title: "OK"` in confirmation dialogs; destructive alerts with no `.cancel` role.

text: Mark a button destructive when it would destroy data the person did not set out to destroy; options that follow from an action they started go in an action sheet (`confirmationDialog`), not an alert or menu.
check: review `role:.destructive` / `.destructive` usage; follow-up choices presented with `.alert`.

text: Match the keyboard to the field and tell the system what the field holds, so AutoFill and suggestions can help (email, phone, one-time code, new password, address).
check: grep `TextField(` / `UITextField` with no `.keyboardType(` and `.textContentType(` (e.g. `.emailAddress`, `.oneTimeCode`, `.newPassword`).

text: Password entry uses a secure field and always starts empty.
check: grep password inputs that are not `SecureField` / `isSecureTextEntry = true`, or that get a default value.

text: When the on-screen keyboard is up, the focused field and its submit control remain visible; position them with the keyboard layout guide.
check: focus the lowest field; if it or the submit button ends up under the keyboard, fail; grep `keyboardLayoutGuide`, `.ignoresSafeArea(.keyboard)`.

text: Set text in system text styles, or scale custom fonts, so it follows Dynamic Type and can grow to at least 200 percent. Reference sizes on iOS/iPadOS: 17 pt default, 11 pt minimum; macOS: 13 pt and 10 pt.
check: grep `.font(.system(size:`, `Font.custom(` without `relativeTo:`, `UIFont.systemFont(ofSize:`, `UIFont(name:` not passed through `UIFontMetrics`; UIKit labels without `adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true`.

text: Large text should not cost content: let labels wrap, and at the largest accessibility size show as much as at the largest standard size.
check: grep `.lineLimit(1)`, `numberOfLines = 1` on body text; Inspector "Clipped text" audit.

text: Icons that carry meaning, and fixed dimensions next to text, grow along with the text size.
check: grep hard-coded `.frame(width:height:)` on icons beside text with no `@ScaledMetric`; SF Symbols already scale.

text: Apple asks for more than VIS-10 (which bans thin weights at small sizes only): set all UI text in Regular weight or heavier, not Ultralight, Thin or Light, and make custom fonts honour Bold Text.
check: grep `.ultraLight`, `.thin`, `.light`; turn on Bold Text and look for custom-font text that stays thin (SwiftUI `legibilityWeight`, UIKit `isBoldTextEnabled`).

text: Follow the system light/dark setting; Apple advises against an in-app appearance switch, and a hard-locked mode makes the app look broken. This is Apple's line; Android and Windows expect a picker (VIS-36).
check: grep `.preferredColorScheme(`, `overrideUserInterfaceStyle`, `UIUserInterfaceStyle` in Info.plist; flip appearance (see Measure). A locked mode fails; a Light/Dark/System picker that defaults to System is a weaker, Apple-only finding.

text: Paint with dynamic system and semantic colors (`label`, `secondaryLabel`, `systemBackground`, grouped backgrounds) rather than fixed values, so Dark Mode, elevated surfaces and Increase Contrast all adapt.
check: grep `Color(red:`, `UIColor(red:`, `Color.white`/`.black` on text, hex helpers; compare light and dark screenshots.

text: Hit the contrast thresholds Accessibility Inspector applies, in light, dark and Increase Contrast: 4.5:1 for text up to 17 pt, 3:1 at 18 pt or in bold. Apple passes bold text of any size at 3:1; WCAG (A11Y-14) wants 4.5:1 for bold under 14 pt, so a finding against WCAG cites A11Y-14.
check: run the Inspector "Contrast" audit in both appearances; it passes small bold text at 3:1, so measure bold text under 14 pt against 4.5:1 yourself.

text: If default colors fall short of contrast, switch to a stronger palette whenever Increase Contrast is on.
check: grep for `colorSchemeContrast` / `isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled` or high-contrast asset-catalog variants; `simctl ui <dev> increase_contrast enabled`, then screenshot.

text: Colour is never the only cue (A11Y-12 owns the rule); on Apple platforms the second cue is a shape, a symbol or words.
check: view a screenshot in grayscale; states that become indistinguishable fail.

text: Draw interface icons from SF Symbols where possible, and give any custom symbol an accessibility label.
check: grep `Image("` asset icons in toolbars and tabs; custom symbols with no `accessibilityLabel`.

text: Every icon-only control and informative image has a label naming its purpose, without the control type (label it "Play", not "Play button").
check: grep `Button` whose label is only an `Image(` and has no `.accessibilityLabel(`; `Image("` with no `Label`/`accessibilityLabel`; Inspector "Element description" audit.

text: Images that are pure decoration are skipped by VoiceOver.
check: grep ornamental `Image(` lacking `.accessibilityHidden(true)` / `Image(decorative:)`; UIKit `isAccessibilityElement`.

text: Give each screen its own distinct title, and flag section headings so the rotor can jump between them.
check: grep `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)` / `.header` trait; screens with no `navigationTitle`.

text: Bundle elements that belong together (a picture and its caption, a cell's parts) so VoiceOver speaks them as one, in a sensible order.
check: grep `.accessibilityElement(children:.combine)` / `shouldGroupAccessibilityChildren` in list cells; swipe through a cell with VoiceOver on.

text: When visible content or layout changes (an error appears, results load), announce it with an accessibility notification.
check: grep `AccessibilityNotification`, `UIAccessibility.post(notification:`; trigger an inline error with VoiceOver running.

text: Custom controls expose correct traits (button, adjustable, selected) and actions, and every gesture has an on-screen equivalent (say, a delete button next to swipe-to-delete).
check: Inspector "Traits" audit; grep `onTapGesture` on views that are not `Button` and lack `.accessibilityAddTraits(.isButton)`.

text: Apple's take on VIS-35: with Reduce Motion on, drop automatic and looping animation (zoom, scale, parallax, depth) and swap sliding transitions for fades; motion is never the sole carrier of information.
check: grep `withAnimation`, `.animation(`, `UIView.animate`, `matchedGeometryEffect` with no `accessibilityReduceMotion` / `isReduceMotionEnabled` check.

text: Photos, video and other media opt out of Smart Invert.
check: grep media views lacking `.accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors()` / `accessibilityIgnoresInvertColors = true`; turn on Smart Invert and screenshot.

text: Ask for a permission at the moment a feature needs it (general rule: WEB-42); asking on launch is only acceptable when the app is useless without it.
check: fresh install (`simctl privacy <dev> reset all`) and launch; a permission prompt before any related action fails; grep `requestAuthorization`, `requestWhenInUseAuthorization`, `requestAccess` in app init/`didFinishLaunching`.

text: Each purpose string is one concrete, complete sentence explaining what the app does with the data.
check: read the `NS*UsageDescription` keys in Info.plist; a generic string like "We need this to work properly" fails.

text: A screen shown before a permission prompt carries a single button, which leads to the system alert and is not labelled "Allow"; before the tracking prompt a custom screen may explain the benefit, but it offers no incentive, does not look like the request, shows no image of the alert and adds no marks pointing at the alert.
check: screenshot pre-prompt screens; an extra "Not now" button or an "Allow" label fails; before tracking, an incentive, a fake alert or arrows at "Allow" fail, a plain explainer with one button passes.

text: Promotional notifications need explicit opt-in and must not use Time Sensitive; the app also offers its own screen for changing notification choices.
check: grep `interruptionLevel =.timeSensitive` on promotional payloads; look for an in-app notification settings screen.

text: Onboarding is short and skippable, teaches inside the real UI, defers optional setup, and holds back rating requests and purchase offers until people have tried the app.
check: count screens before the first real content; a rating prompt or paywall on first run fails.

text: Get to the first screen fast, behind a launch screen that looks almost exactly like it, with no text or advertising, in the current orientation and appearance.
check: record the launch (`simctl io booted recordVideo`); a visible jump between launch screen and first screen fails.

text: Provide the standard menus in their usual order (App, File, Edit, Format where the app edits formatted text, View, app menus, Window, Help), keep a Window menu with Minimize and Zoom even with one window, and wire up the standard shortcuts. Fixed item lists and ellipses: DESK-15.
check: screenshot the menu bar; open the Window menu; a missing or reordered standard menu fails.

text: Settings open from App menu > Settings... (Cmd-Comma) in a window whose minimize and maximize buttons are dimmed, with a fixed toolbar, a title naming the current pane, and the last-viewed pane reopened.
check: press Cmd-Comma; a settings button in the main toolbar, or a resizable settings window, fails.

text: General public: aim no higher than a reading age of 9; the UK Home Office keeps that ceiling for specialist readers as well. In US grades, NN/g puts general audiences at 6th-8th grade and a broad consumer audience at 8th grade.
check: score each screen (Measure); for UK public-sector or GOV.UK-style products flag anything above grade 4 (reading age 9 by the conversion table the Home Office links ), for other general-public products anything above grade 8 (NN/g).

text: Lower-literacy readers (public services, health, benefits, mass-market products): 6th grade on the homepage, main category pages and landing pages, 8th grade on the rest; lead with the main point, keep one column and static text, because these readers go through text word by word instead of skimming.
check: grade by page type; key pages with two text columns or content reachable only through fly-out menus.

text: Professionals and experts (B2B, clinical, legal, developer tools): 10th-12th grade is fine; beyond 12th grade even highly educated readers have to work too hard. Experts still prefer short, skimmable text, and GOV.UK reports that highly literate readers favour plain English too, so "our users are experts" never justifies dense copy.
check: any screen scoring above grade 12; long unbroken paragraphs in expert tools.

text: Experts: keep a technical term only when you are sure this audience knows it, and move explanations meant for secondary readers into another layer (link, tooltip, glossary) so they do not slow down the main flow.
check: unexplained acronyms during onboarding; inline definitions experts must wade through on every visit.

text: Children: match each child's own school grade and design for one narrow age band (3-5, 6-8 or 9-12); NN/g saw children reject content pitched one grade off their own and skip long blocks of instructions.
check: a single set of copy aimed at ages 3 to 12; instructions longer than a few lines.

text: Readers with cognitive or learning disabilities (health, care, public services, any WCAG AAA target): apply TEXT-12, TEXT-13, TEXT-19, TEXT-32 and TEXT-46. Where text demands more than lower secondary education (7-9 years of schooling), offer supplemental content or an easier version (WCAG 3.1.5, AAA).
check: long or complex text with no summary, illustration or easy-read alternative next to it.

text: Break up any sentence longer than 25 words (GOV.UK); NN/g targets roughly 15-20 words.
check: words per sentence from Measure; list each sentence above 25 words.

text: Give each sentence a single idea; when a sentence carries subordinate clauses or exceptions, split them into sentences of their own.
check: sentences chained with repeated and/or/but, or carrying except, unless, provided that.

text: Keep paragraphs to 5 sentences or fewer (GOV.UK), each about one topic and opening with it. digital.gov sets 150 words as the usual ceiling and 250 words as the absolute limit.
check: count sentences and words per paragraph.

text: Prefer active voice so the reader can see who does what; passive is acceptable where the law makes one step follow another. Use indicative mood in explanations and imperative in procedures.
check: read for passives with no actor (is/are/was/were/be/been + past participle); steps written as descriptions instead of commands.

text: Prefer present tense and plain verbs; turn nouns built from verbs back into verbs ("make a decision" becomes "decide", "provide assistance" becomes "help").
check: grep `(make|provide|perform|conduct) (a |an )?\w+(ion|ment|ance)` for candidates, then read.

text: Pick short everyday words over formal ones ("buy" over "purchase", "use" over "utilise/utilize", "start" over "commence"; delete "in order to"). COGA points to the 1500 most common words as a vocabulary guide.
check: run the GOV.UK words-to-avoid list and the digital.gov substitution table against the locale files.

text: Keep sentence structure simple: state positives without double negatives and do not nest one clause inside another.
check: grep `not (un|in|dis)\w+` and `cannot not`; read for "not... unless".

text: Talk to the reader directly as "you".
check: text about the reader that says "the user", "users" or "customers".

text: Explain a specialist term at its first appearance and leave out buzzwords. For words used in a special or narrow sense, idioms and jargon included, offer a way to find the definition (WCAG 3.1.3): inline at first use, a linked definition or a glossary.
check: a term that appears before its definition, or never gets one.

text: Write about half as many words as print would use; in NN/g testing, concise text scored 58% better and the concise, scannable and objective version 124% better.
check: welcome text and empty states that restate what the interface already shows.

text: Stay objective and drop promotional adjectives: objective wording tested 27% better, and GOV.UK warns that adjectives make text sound emotive and like spin.
check: powerful, "seamless", "simply", "easy", "world-class" on task screens.

text: Leave "please" and "please note" out of instructions.
check: grep -i `please note|please`.

text: Say things literally and concretely; if a metaphor or simile stays, explain it.
check: read for idioms such as "ballpark", "touch base", "under the hood".

text: Lead with what matters most (inverted pyramid): the conclusion opens the page and each paragraph opens with its key sentence. Most people skim: NN/g found 79% of test users always scanned a new page and 16% read word by word, and GOV.UK says users read 20-28% of a page.
check: the screen's main answer or action comes only after background text.

text: Get the key points into the first two paragraphs.
check: screenshot; the key point sits after paragraph 2 or below the fold.

text: Write headings that describe their section: no generic ones ("Introduction", "Overview", "Details"), no questions, and the most informative words first so the opening two words identify the section.
check: list every h2-h4; flag generic, clever or question headings.

text: Give the page one H1 as its title with H2-H4 beneath; the text must make sense even if the headings are removed.
check: `document.querySelectorAll('h1').length !== 1`; skipped heading levels.

text: Turn sets of items and processes into bulleted or numbered lists, and replace complex sentences and paragraphs with lists or tables.
check: a sentence that runs through 3+ items or steps inline.

text: Open long pages with a summary, and do not restate it in the first paragraph.
check: help or docs pages without a summary, or with the summary repeated.

text: Let link text name the destination or action, with the relevant words first; avoid "click here", "more" and "learn more"; a one-word link needs a word of 3 or more syllables.
check: grep link text `>(click here|here|more|learn more|read more)<`.

text: Do not make text depend on seeing the layout ("in the sidebar", "the button on the right", "see below").
check: grep -i `(sidebar|on the (left|right)|above|below|red|green) `.

text: Name each concept with one word throughout, and never reuse one word for two concepts.
check: build a term list from the locale files (e.g. "workspace/project/space", "delete/remove", "sign in/log in") and flag synonyms for the same object or action.

text: Use the readers' vocabulary rather than the team's: choose the word the audience knows best and the words they would type into a search engine; swap invented brand names for plain terms, or at least pair them.
check: product-coined nouns in navigation and headings with no plain-word gloss.

text: Do not coin words or stretch existing words to new meanings.
